title.zh: 卷四十三 列傳第三十三 齊高帝諸子下
title.en: Volume 43 Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 2
title.raw: 卷四十三 列傳第三十三 齊高帝諸子下 Volume 43 Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 2

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十三齊高帝諸子下

translations.literal: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part Two

sentences.zh: 臨川獻王映字宣光，高帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Linchuan, Ying, style name Xuangguang, was the third son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Prince Xian of Linchuan, whose style name was Xuangguang, was Emperor Gao's third son.

sentences.zh: 少而警悟，美言笑，善容止。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick-witted; his speech and smile were pleasing, and his bearing was graceful.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was remarkably perceptive, with a pleasing voice and smile and elegant deportment.

sentences.zh: 仕宋位給事黃門侍郎、南兗州刺史，留心吏事，自下莫不肅然，令行禁止。

translations.literal: He served in Song as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou; he devoted attention to official business, and from the lowest ranks upward all were in awe—his orders were carried out and his prohibitions enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he served as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou; attentive to administrative affairs, he inspired respect from the lowest clerk upward, and his commands were obeyed without exception.

sentences.zh: 高帝踐阼，為荊州刺史，加都督，封臨川王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he was made Inspector of Jingzhou with the added title of supreme commander and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Jingzhou with supreme command authority and enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗致錢還都買物，有獻計者，於江陵買貨，至都還換，可得微有所增。

translations.literal: He once sent money back to the capital to buy goods; someone suggested buying merchandise at Jiangling and exchanging it at the capital for a small profit.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent funds to the capital to purchase goods; an adviser proposed buying merchandise at Jiangling and reselling it in the capital for a modest gain.

sentences.zh: 映笑曰：「我是賈客邪，乃復求利。

translations.literal: Ying laughed and said, "Am I a merchant, that I should seek profit again?
translations.idiomatic: Ying laughed and said, "Am I a merchant, that I should go seeking profit?

sentences.zh: 」改授都督、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was reassigned as supreme commander and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then reassigned as supreme commander and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒞事聰敏，府州曹局皆重足以奉禁令，自宋彭城王義康以後，未之有也。

translations.literal: He was sharp in attending to affairs; all the bureaus of the prefecture and province walked on tiptoe to obey his prohibitions—there had been nothing like it since Prince Yikang of Pengcheng under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally capable in office; every bureau in the prefecture and province trod lightly to heed his orders—nothing comparable had been seen since Prince Yikang of Pengcheng in the Song.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，為侍中、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he became Palace Attendant and Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed Palace Attendant and Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 五年，即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he received the precedent title of Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was granted the status of Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 七年薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 映善騎射，解聲律，工左右書、左右射，應接賓客，風韻韶靡，及薨，朝野莫不惋惜。

translations.literal: Ying excelled at mounted archery, understood music theory, and was skilled in both-handed writing and ambidextrous shooting; when receiving guests his elegance was refined and graceful, and at his death court and populace alike mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was skilled in horsemanship and archery, versed in musical theory, and adept at writing and shooting with either hand; in receiving guests his manner was graceful and refined. At his death, court and country alike grieved.

sentences.zh: 贈司空。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the office of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 九子皆封侯。

translations.literal: All nine of his sons were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: All nine of his sons were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 長子子晉，永元初為侍中，入梁為高平太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zijin served as Palace Attendant at the beginning of Yongyuan; when Liang was established he became Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zijin served as Palace Attendant at the start of the Yongyuan era; after the Liang dynasty was founded he became Administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 第二子子遊，州陵侯，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: The second son, Ziyou, Marquis of Zhouling, was a Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Ziyou, Marquis of Zhouling, served as Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 謀反，兄弟並伏誅。

translations.literal: They plotted rebellion and both brothers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted rebellion, and both brothers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 長沙威王晃字宣明，高帝第四子也。

translations.literal: Huang, Prince Wei of Changsha, style name Xuanming, was the fourth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, Prince Wei of Changsha, whose style name was Xuanming, was Emperor Gao's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 少有武力，為高帝所愛。

translations.literal: From youth he had martial prowess and was beloved by Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he showed martial prowess and was a favorite of Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，代兄映為淮南、宣城二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he replaced his elder brother Ying as Administrator of the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming he succeeded his elder brother Ying as Administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 晃便弓馬，初沈攸之事起，晃多從武容，赫弈都街，時人為之語曰：「煥煥蕭四傘。

translations.literal: Huang was skilled with bow and horse; when Shen Youzhi's rebellion first arose, Huang often followed with martial retinue, dazzling the capital streets, and people made a saying about him: "Brilliant, brilliant—Xiao the Fourth with his parasol.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was adept with bow and horse; when Shen Youzhi's rebellion first broke out, Huang often rode out with a martial escort, dazzling the streets of the capital, and people coined a saying: "Splendid, splendid—Young Master Xiao the Fourth and his parasol.

sentences.zh: 」其年，遷西中郎將、豫州刺史，監二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: " That same year he was transferred to Western Central Army General and Inspector of Yuzhou, supervising military affairs of the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: " That same year he was promoted to Western Central Army General and Inspector of Yuzhou, with authority over military affairs in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 高帝踐阼，晃每陳政事，輒為典簽所裁，晃殺之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Huang often presented matters of state but was always overruled by the record-keeper; Huang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gao took the throne, Huang frequently submitted policy proposals, only to have them blocked by his chief clerk; Huang killed the man.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，手詔賜杖。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and personally wrote an edict bestowing beating-sticks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent a personal edict ordering that he be beaten with staves.

sentences.zh: 遷南徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Southern Xuzhou with the added title of supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Southern Xuzhou with supreme command authority.

sentences.zh: 武帝為皇太子，拜武進陵，于曲阿後湖鬥隊，使晃御馬軍，上聞之，又不悅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was crown prince and paid respects at Wujin Mausoleum, at the rear lake of Qu'e they held chariot-team competitions; he had Huang command the cavalry, and when the emperor heard of it he was again displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was crown prince and visited Wujin Mausoleum, chariot teams competed on the rear lake at Qu'e; he had Huang lead the cavalry wing. When the emperor heard of this, he was displeased once again.

sentences.zh: 臨崩，以晃屬武帝，處以輦轂近蕃，勿令遠出。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he entrusted Huang to Emperor Wu, placing him as a close prince in the capital region and instructing that he not be sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he entrusted Huang to Emperor Wu, keeping him as a prince near the capital and instructing that he not be posted far away.

sentences.zh: 後拜車騎將軍、侍中。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Chariot Cavalry General and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Chariot Cavalry General and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the status of Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗幸鍾山，晃從駕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once visited Mount Zhong; Huang accompanied the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once visited Mount Zhong, and Huang accompanied the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 以馬矟刺道邊枯櫱，上令左右數人引之，銀纏皆卷聚而矟不出，乃令晃復馳馬拔之，應手便去。

translations.literal: He stabbed a withered stump by the roadside with his cavalry lance; the emperor had several attendants try to pull it out—the silver wrappings all wound together but the lance would not come free—then he had Huang charge again and draw it out; it came away at once in his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He drove his cavalry lance into a withered stump by the road; the emperor had several attendants try to pull it free, but the silver bindings wound tight and the lance would not budge. He then had Huang charge again and wrench it out—it came free instantly in his grip.

sentences.zh: 每遠州獻駿馬，上輒令晃于華林中調試之。

translations.literal: Whenever distant provinces presented fine horses, the emperor always had Huang test and train them in the Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever distant provinces presented fine horses, the emperor always had Huang break and train them in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 高帝常曰：「此我家任城也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao often said, "This one is our family's Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao often said, "This one is our family's own Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 」武帝緣此意，故諡曰威。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu followed this sentiment, and therefore his posthumous name was Wei (Martial).
translations.idiomatic: " Drawing on this sentiment, Emperor Wu gave him the posthumous title Wei (Martial).

sentences.zh: 武陵昭王曄字宣昭，高帝第五子也。

translations.literal: Ye, Prince Zhao of Wuling, style name Xuanzhao, was the fifth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, Prince Zhao of Wuling, whose style name was Xuanzhao, was Emperor Gao's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 母羅氏，從高帝在淮陰，以罪誅。

translations.literal: His mother was the Luo clan; she followed Emperor Gao at Huaiyin and was executed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Luo clan, had accompanied Emperor Gao at Huaiyin and was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 曄年四歲，思慕不異成人，每慟吐血。

translations.literal: When Ye was four years old his longing for her was no different from an adult's; each time he grieved he coughed up blood.
translations.idiomatic: At four years old Ye's grief for her was as deep as any adult's; each time he mourned he coughed up blood.

sentences.zh: 高帝敕武帝曰：「三昧至性如此，恐不濟，汝可與共住，每抑割之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao charged Emperor Wu: "Sanmei has such extreme nature—he may not survive; you should live with him together and always restrain and curb him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao instructed Emperor Wu: "Sanmei's nature is so extreme that he may not survive; you should live with him and always restrain him.

sentences.zh: 」三昧，曄小字也。

translations.literal: " Sanmei was Ye's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Sanmei was Ye's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 故曄見愛。

translations.literal: Therefore Ye was cherished.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Ye was especially cherished.

sentences.zh: 高帝雖為方伯，而居處甚貧，諸子學書無紙筆，曄常以指畫空中及畫掌學字，遂工篆法。

translations.literal: Although Emperor Gao was a regional governor, his dwelling was very poor; the sons had no paper or brush to study writing—Ye often traced characters in the air with his finger and on his palm to learn, and thus mastered seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Gao held a regional governorship, the household was desperately poor; the sons had no paper or brushes for study—Ye traced characters in the air and on his palm to practice writing, and eventually mastered seal script.

sentences.zh: 少時又無棋局，乃破荻為片，縱橫以為棋局，指點行勢，遂至名品。

translations.literal: In youth he also had no chess board, so he broke reeds into strips and laid them crosswise as a board, pointing out moves and positions, until he reached master rank.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he had no chessboard either, so he split reeds into strips and laid them crosswise to make one, calling out moves and positions until he reached master rank.

sentences.zh: 性剛穎俊出，與諸王共作短句詩，學謝靈運體，以呈高帝。

translations.literal: His nature was firm, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he composed short-verse poems in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them to Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was bold, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he wrote short poems in the manner of Xie Lingyun and presented them to Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中，最為優者。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Seeing your twenty characters—among all the boys' compositions yours is the finest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I have seen your twenty lines—among all my sons' compositions, yours is the finest.

sentences.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑其次也。」

translations.literal: But Xie Kangyue is unrestrained; his compositional form does not distinguish beginning from end. Pan Anren and Lu Shiheng are deeply worthy of reverence; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."
translations.idiomatic: But Kangyue is unrestrained—his compositions lack clear structure from beginning to end. Anren and Shiheng are truly worthy of emulation; Yanzhi ranks below them."

sentences.zh: 建元二年，為會稽太守，加都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he became Administrator of Kuaiji with the added title of supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan he was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji with supreme command authority.

sentences.zh: 上遣儒士劉瓛往郡，為曄講五經。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Confucian scholar Liu Huan to the commandery to lecture Ye on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the scholar Liu Huan to the commandery to instruct Ye in the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，曆中書令、祠部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Ye successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Rites for the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Ye served successively as Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Rites for the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 巫覡或言曄有非常之相，以此自負，武帝聞之，故無寵，未嘗處方嶽。

translations.literal: Shamans or diviners sometimes said Ye had the countenance of one extraordinary; relying on this he grew proud; Emperor Wu heard of it and therefore showed him no favor—he was never placed in a major provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans and diviners sometimes claimed Ye bore the marks of an extraordinary destiny; he grew proud on this account. When Emperor Wu heard of it, he withheld favor and never assigned Ye to a major provincial governorship.

sentences.zh: 于御坐曲宴，醉伏地，貂抄肉柈。

translations.literal: At an informal banquet on the imperial seat, drunk he collapsed to the floor, his sable fur brushing the meat tray.
translations.idiomatic: At an informal banquet before the emperor, he collapsed drunk to the floor, his sable robe sweeping the meat platter.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「汙貂。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "You've soiled the sable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "You've soiled your sable.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下愛其羽毛，而疏其骨肉。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your Majesty cherishes its fur but neglects its flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Your Majesty cherishes the fur but neglects the flesh and bone.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 性輕財重義，有古人風。

translations.literal: His nature valued righteousness over wealth and had the air of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: He valued righteousness over wealth and bore the spirit of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 罷會稽還都，齋中錢不滿萬，俸祿所入，皆與參佐賓僚共之。

translations.literal: When he left Kuaiji and returned to the capital, the money in his study did not amount to ten thousand; everything from his salary he shared with staff and guest officials.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Kuaiji and returned to the capital, he had fewer than ten thousand coins in his study; he shared all his salary income with his staff and guests.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「兄作天子，何畏弟無錢。

translations.literal: He often said, "With an elder brother as Son of Heaven, why should a younger brother fear having no money?
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "With an elder brother as Son of Heaven, why should a younger brother worry about money?

sentences.zh: 」居止附身所須而已。

translations.literal: " He kept only what he needed for his person.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept only what he needed for daily life.

sentences.zh: 名後堂山為首陽，蓋怨貧薄也。

translations.literal: He named the hill behind his hall Mount Shouyang—as a complaint of his poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He named the hill behind his hall Mount Shouyang—a bitter joke about his poverty.

sentences.zh: 嘗于武帝前與竟陵王子良圍棋，子良大北。

translations.literal: He once played Go before Emperor Wu with Ziliang, Prince of Jingling; Ziliang lost badly.
translations.idiomatic: He once played Go before Emperor Wu against Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, and Ziliang suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 及退，豫章文獻王謂曄曰：「汝與司徒手談，故當小相推讓。

translations.literal: When they withdrew, the Prince of Yuzhang said to Ye: "When you play the Minister of State at the board, you ought to yield a little.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, the Prince of Yuzhang said to Ye: "When you play the Minister of State at the board, you ought to yield a little.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「曄立身以來，未嘗一口妄語。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Since Ye took his stand in life, he has never once spoken falsely.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Since I took my stand in life, I have never once spoken falsely.

sentences.zh: 」執心疏婞，偏不知悔。

translations.literal: " His disposition was blunt and unyielding; he simply knew no regret.
translations.idiomatic: " His disposition was blunt and unyielding; he simply knew no regret.

sentences.zh: 好文章，射為當時獨絕，琅邪王瞻亦稱善射，而不及曄也。

translations.literal: He loved literature; in archery he was unrivaled in his time—Wang Zhan of Langye was also praised for shooting but could not match Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He loved literature; in archery he was unrivaled in his day—Wang Zhan of Langye was also praised as an archer but could not match Ye.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸豫章王嶷東田，宴諸長王，獨不召曄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu visited the eastern fields of Prince Yuzhang and feasted the elder princes, not summoning Ye alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu visited the eastern fields of the Prince of Yuzhang and feasted the elder princes, deliberately not summoning Ye.

sentences.zh: 嶷曰：「風景殊美，今日甚憶武陵。

translations.literal: Ying said, "The scenery is exceptionally fine—today I miss Prince Wuling greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "The scenery is exceptionally fine—today I miss Prince Wuling sorely.

sentences.zh: 」上仍呼使射，屢發命中，顧四坐曰：「手何如？

translations.literal: " The emperor still summoned him to shoot; shot after shot hit the mark; he looked around the assembly and said, "How is my hand?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still summoned Ye to shoot; arrow after arrow hit the mark. Ye looked around the assembly and said, "How is my hand?

sentences.zh: 」上神色甚怪，嶷曰：「阿五常日不爾，今可謂仰藉天威。

translations.literal: " The emperor's expression was very strange; Ying said, "Younger brother Wu is not usually like this—today one might say he borrows Heaven's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's expression turned strange. The prince said, "Younger brother Wu is not usually like this—today one might say he draws on Heaven's majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃釋。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mood then eased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's mood then eased.

sentences.zh: 後於華林射賭，凡六箭，五破一皮，賜錢五萬文。

translations.literal: Later at Hualin Park in an archery wager, of six arrows five pierced one hide; he was given fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Hualin Park in an archery contest, of six arrows five pierced a single hide; he was awarded fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 又上舉酒勸曄，曰：「陛下常不以此處許臣。

translations.literal: Again the emperor raised wine to toast Ye, and Ye said, "Your Majesty does not usually grant me such a place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again raised his cup to toast Ye, and Ye said, "Your Majesty does not usually grant me such a place of honor.

sentences.zh: 」上回面不答。

translations.literal: " The emperor turned his face away without answering.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor turned away without answering.

sentences.zh: 豫章王于邸起土山，列種桐竹，號為桐山。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang at his residence raised an earthen hill and planted paulownia and bamboo in rows, calling it Mount Tong.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence the Prince of Yuzhang built an earthen hill and planted paulownia and bamboo in rows, naming it Mount Tong.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸之，置酒為樂，顧臨川王映：「王邸亦有嘉名不？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu visited it, set out wine for pleasure, and turned to Prince Ying of Linchuan: "Does your residence also have a fine name?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu visited and set out wine for pleasure, then turned to Prince Ying of Linchuan: "Does your residence also have a fine name?

sentences.zh: 」映曰：「臣好棲靜，因以為稱。

translations.literal: " Ying said, "Your servant loves tranquil dwelling, and thus takes that as his name.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying said, "Your servant loves quiet seclusion, and so I take that as my name.

sentences.zh: 」又問曄，曄曰：「臣山卑，不曾棲靈昭景，唯有薇蕨，直號首陽山。

translations.literal: " They asked Ye again; Ye said, "Your servant's hill is low—it has never housed spiritual brightness and splendid vistas, only bracken and ferns; I simply call it Mount Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: " They asked Ye next; Ye said, "Your servant's hill is low—it has never sheltered spirits or splendid vistas, only bracken and ferns; I simply call it Mount Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此直勞者之歌也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "That is simply a laborer's song."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That is simply a laborer's lament."

sentences.zh: 久之，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was sent out as Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was sent out as Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以曄方出鎮，求其宅給諸皇子，遣舍人喻旨。

translations.literal: Because Ye had just gone out to command a province, the emperor sought his residence to give to other princes and sent a palace secretary to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Ye had just departed to take up his provincial command, the emperor sought his residence to give to other princes and sent a palace secretary to convey his wishes.

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「先帝賜臣此宅，使臣歌哭有所，陛下欲以州易宅，臣請不以宅易州。

translations.literal: Ye said, "The former emperor gave me this residence so I would have a place to sing and weep; if Your Majesty wishes to trade a province for the house, your servant asks not to trade the house for a province.
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "The former emperor gave me this residence so I would have a place to mourn and rejoice; if Your Majesty wishes to trade a province for this house, I ask not to trade the house for a province.

sentences.zh: 」帝恨之。

translations.literal: " The emperor resented this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 至鎮百餘日，典簽趙渥之啟曄得失，征還為左戶尚書。

translations.literal: After reaching his post for a little over a hundred days, the record-keeper Zhao Wozhi reported Ye's faults and merits; he was recalled and made Minister of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a hundred days at his post, chief clerk Zhao Wozhi reported on Ye's conduct; he was recalled and appointed Minister of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 累不得志。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he failed to achieve his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he failed to achieve his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 冬節問訊，諸王皆出，曄獨後來，上已還便殿，聞曄至，引見，問之，曄稱牛羸不能取路。

translations.literal: At the winter festival audience all the princes set out; Ye alone came late—the emperor had already returned to the side hall; hearing Ye had arrived, he summoned him and questioned him; Ye said his ox was weak and could not find the way.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter festival audience all the princes set out; Ye alone arrived late. The emperor had already returned to the side hall; hearing Ye had come, he summoned him and questioned the delay. Ye said his ox was weak and could not keep to the road.

sentences.zh: 上敕車府給副禦牛一頭。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chariot bureau to provide one alternate imperial ox.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chariot bureau to provide a spare imperial ox.

sentences.zh: 敕主客自今諸王來不隨例者，不復為通。

translations.literal: He charged the chief receptionist that from now on princes who did not follow protocol would no longer be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the chief receptionist that from then on princes who failed to observe protocol would no longer be admitted.

sentences.zh: 公事還，過竟陵王子良宅，冬月道逢乞人，脫襦與之。

translations.literal: Returning from official business he passed the residence of Prince Ziliang of Jingling; in winter on the road he met a beggar and took off his padded coat to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from official business he passed the residence of the Prince of Jingling; in the depths of winter he met a beggar on the road and stripped off his padded coat to give him.

sentences.zh: 子良見曄衣單，進襦於曄。

translations.literal: Ziliang saw Ye lightly dressed and offered him a padded coat.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang saw Ye thinly clad and offered him a padded coat.

sentences.zh: 曄曰：「我與向人亦復何異。

translations.literal: Ye said, "What difference is there between me and the man I just gave to?
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "What difference is there between me and the man I just gave it to?

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王儉詣曄，曄留儉設食，盤中菘菜鱯魚而已。

translations.literal: " Minister Wang Jian visited Ye; Ye kept him for a meal—with only cabbage and catfish in the dishes.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister Wang Jian called on Ye; Ye kept him for a meal of nothing but cabbage and catfish.

sentences.zh: 儉重其率真，為飽食盡歡而去。

translations.literal: Jian valued his straightforward sincerity and ate his fill, enjoying themselves fully before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Jian valued his unvarnished sincerity, ate his fill, and departed in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 安成恭王暠字宣曜，高帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Gao, Prince Gong of Ancheng, style name Xuanyao, was the sixth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, Prince Gong of Ancheng, whose style name was Xuanyao, was Emperor Gao's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 性清和，多疾。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and clear, and he was often ill.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was gentle and mild, and he was frequently ill.

sentences.zh: 歷位南中郎將、江州刺史，侍中，領步兵校尉，中書令。

translations.literal: He successively held Southern Central Army General, Inspector of Jiangzhou, Palace Attendant, Colonel of Footsoldiers, and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Southern Central Army General, Inspector of Jiangzhou, Palace Attendant, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，為散騎常侍、秘書監，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming he was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat Archives, and in charge of garrison affairs at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat Archives, with charge of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 及夏薨。

translations.literal: He died in summer.
translations.idiomatic: He died that summer.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王鏘字宣韶，高帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Qiang, Prince of Poyang, style name Xuanshao, was the seventh son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang, Prince of Poyang, whose style name was Xuanshao, was Emperor Gao's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 建元末，武帝即位，為雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianyuan, when Emperor Wu took the throne, he was Inspector of Yongzhou with the added title of supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianyuan era, when Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou with supreme command authority.

sentences.zh: 武帝服除，鏘方還，始入覲拜便流涕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu's mourning period ended, Qiang had just returned; on his first audience and bow he burst into tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's mourning period ended, Qiang had only just returned; at his first audience he bowed and burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 武帝愕然，問其故，鏘收淚曰：「臣違奉彌年，今奉顏色，聖顏損瘦，所以泣耳。

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and asked the reason; Qiang wiped away his tears and said, "Your servant has been away from attendance for many years; now I behold Your Majesty's countenance. The sacred visage has grown thin—that is why I weep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken aback and asked why; Qiang dried his tears and said, "I have been absent from Your Majesty for many years; now I see your face again. Your sacred visage has grown thin—that is why I weep.

sentences.zh: 」武帝歎曰：「我復是有此一弟。」

translations.literal: " The emperor sighed and said, "I still have such a brother as this."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed and said, "I still have a brother like this."

sentences.zh: 累遷丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming he became General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongming he was appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 鏘和悌美令，性謙慎，好文章，有寵于武帝。

translations.literal: Qiang was harmonious, agreeable, and handsome in bearing, of a modest and cautious nature, fond of literature, and favored by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang was gentle, agreeable, and handsome, modest and cautious by nature, fond of literature, and in favor with Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 領軍之授，齊室諸王所未為，鏘在官理事無壅，當時稱之。

translations.literal: The appointment as General of the Guards had never been given to a prince of the Qi house; Qiang handled official business without backlog, and at the time he was praised for it.
translations.idiomatic: The post of General of the Guards had never before been held by a prince of the Qi house; Qiang conducted affairs without backlog and was praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 車駕游幸，常甲仗衛從，恩待次豫章王嶷。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went on tour, he was regularly escorted by armed guards; his gracious treatment ranked second only to the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours he was regularly escorted by armed guards; in favor he ranked just below the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 其年，給油絡車。

translations.literal: That year he was given a lacquered carriage with an oiled canopy.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was granted a lacquered carriage with an oiled canopy.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，轉尚書左僕射，遷侍中、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, then promoted to Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry General, and Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes, with troops stationed and aides appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry General, and Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes, with troops and staff assigned.

sentences.zh: 鏘雍容得物情，為郁林依信。

translations.literal: Qiang was easy and gracious and won popular sentiment; Emperor Yulin relied on and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang was easy in manner and won popular affection; Emperor Yulin trusted and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 郁林心疑明帝，諸王問訊，獨留鏘，謂曰：「聞鸞於法身何如？

translations.literal: Yulin harbored suspicions of Emperor Ming; when the princes came for their audience, he alone kept Qiang and said, "What have you heard of Luan's intentions toward the Dharma Body?
translations.idiomatic: Yulin suspected Emperor Ming; when the princes came to pay respects, he alone detained Qiang and said, "What have you heard of Luan's attitude toward the Dharma Body?

sentences.zh: 」鏘曰：「臣鸞于宗戚最長，且受寄先帝，臣等年皆尚少，朝廷之幹，唯鸞一人，願陛下無以為慮。

translations.literal: " Qiang said, "Your servant: among the imperial clan Luan is the eldest, and he received the former emperor's trust. We are all still young; the pillar of the court is Luan alone. I hope Your Majesty will not worry on this account.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiang said, "Among the imperial kin Luan is the eldest, and he received the former emperor's trust. We are all still young; Luan alone is the pillar of the court. I hope Your Majesty will not worry about him.

sentences.zh: 」郁林退謂徐龍駒曰：「我欲與公共計取鸞，公既不同，我不能獨辦，且復小聽。

translations.literal: " Yulin withdrew and said to Xu Longju, "I wish to join with you in a plan to take Luan; since you do not agree, I cannot act alone—let us wait a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: " Yulin withdrew and told Xu Longju, "I want to join with you in a plot against Luan; since you disagree, I cannot act alone—for now let us wait a little longer.

sentences.zh: 」及郁林廢，鏘竟不知。

translations.literal: " When Yulin was deposed, Qiang did not know of it at all.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yulin was deposed, Qiang knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，進位司徒，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was promoted to Minister of State, remaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he was promoted to Minister of State while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明帝鎮東府，權威稍異，鏘每往，明帝屣履至車迎鏘，語及家國，言淚俱下，鏘以此推信之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming held the eastern residence and his authority gradually differed from others'; whenever Qiang came, Ming ran out in slippers to his carriage to welcome Qiang; speaking of family and state, words and tears flowed together, and Qiang therefore trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming held the eastern residence and his power grew distinct; whenever Qiang visited, Ming would run out in slippers to meet his carriage. Speaking of family and state, they wept together, and Qiang came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 而宮台內皆屬意於鏘，勸令入宮，發兵輔政。

translations.literal: Yet within the palace all looked to Qiang and urged him to enter the palace and raise troops to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the palace many looked to Qiang and urged him to enter the palace and raise troops to take charge of government.

sentences.zh: 制局監謝粲說鏘及隨王子隆曰：「殿下但乘油壁車入宮，出天子置朝堂，二王夾輔號令，粲等閉城門上仗，誰敢不同，宣城公政當投井求活，豈有一步動哉！

translations.literal: The Control Bureau supervisor Xie Can urged Qiang and the Prince of Sui, Zilong, saying, "Your Highness need only ride the lacquered carriage into the palace, bring out the Son of Heaven and set him in the hall of audience, with the two kings flanking him to issue commands; Can and the rest will shut the gates and man the ramparts—who would dare disagree? The Prince of Xuancheng would only throw himself down a well to beg for his life—he could not move a single step!
translations.idiomatic: Control Bureau supervisor Xie Can urged Qiang and Prince Zilong of Sui: "Your Highness need only ride the lacquered carriage into the palace, bring out the Son of Heaven to the audience hall, with the two kings flanking him to issue orders; we will shut the gates and man the walls—who would dare refuse? The Prince of Xuancheng would only throw himself down a well to beg his life—he could not stir a single step!

sentences.zh: 東城人政共縳送耳。

translations.literal: The people of the eastern city would just bind him and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the eastern quarter would simply bind him and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 」子隆欲定計，鏘以上臺兵力既悉東府，且慮難捷，意甚猶豫。

translations.literal: " Zilong wished to settle on a plan; Qiang, because the capital's military strength was already entirely at the eastern residence and he also feared success would be hard to achieve, was very hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: " Zilong wished to fix on a plan; Qiang, seeing that the capital's forces were already entirely at the eastern residence and fearing the coup might not succeed, was deeply hesitant.

sentences.zh: 馬隊主劉巨，武帝時舊人，詣鏘請間，叩頭勸鏘立事。

translations.literal: The cavalry detachment chief Liu Ju, an old retainer from Emperor Wu's time, came to Qiang requesting a private audience and kowtowed to urge Qiang to act.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry detachment chief Liu Ju, a veteran from Emperor Wu's day, sought a private audience with Qiang and kowtowed to urge him to act.

sentences.zh: 鏘命駕將入，復回還內，與母陸太妃別，日暮不成行。

translations.literal: Qiang ordered his carriage prepared to enter the palace, then turned back inside to take leave of his mother, Grand Consort Lu; by evening he had still not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang ordered his carriage to enter the palace, then went back inside to bid farewell to his mother, Grand Consort Lu; by nightfall he still had not departed.

sentences.zh: 典簽知謀告之，數日，明帝遣二千人圍鏘宅，害鏘，謝粲等皆見殺。

translations.literal: The record-keeper learned of the plot and reported it; within days Emperor Ming sent two thousand men to surround Qiang's residence and killed him; Xie Can and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk learned of the plot and reported it; within days Emperor Ming sent two thousand men to surround Qiang's residence and killed him; Xie Can and the others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 凡諸王被害，皆以夜遣兵圍宅，或斧斫關排牆，叫噪而入，家財皆見封籍焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the princes were killed, troops were sent at night to surround their residences, sometimes chopping through gates or battering down walls, shouting as they burst in; household property was all sealed and inventoried.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever princes were killed, troops were sent at night to surround their residences, sometimes hacking through gates or battering down walls, shouting as they rushed in; all household property was sealed and inventoried.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王鑠字宣朗，高帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Shuo, Prince of Guiyang, style name Xuanlang, was the eighth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, Prince of Guiyang, whose style name was Xuanlang, was Emperor Gao's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 永明七年為中書令，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he became Director of the Secretariat with the added title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongming he was appointed Director of the Secretariat with the added rank of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時鄱陽王鏘好文章，鑠好名理，人稱為鄱桂。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Qiang of Poyang loved literature and Shuo loved principles of names and reality; people called them Poyang and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Qiang of Poyang loved literature and Shuo loved philosophical principle; people called them "Poyang and Guiyang."

sentences.zh: 鑠清羸有冷疾，常枕臥，武帝臨視，賜床帳衾褥。

translations.literal: Shuo was slight and frail with a chronic cold ailment and often lay abed; Emperor Wu visited him in person and bestowed bed curtains and quilts.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was slight and frail with a chronic cold disorder and often kept to his bed; Emperor Wu visited him in person and bestowed bedding and quilts.

sentences.zh: 性理偏詖，遇其賞興，則詩酒連日，情有所廢，則兄弟不通。

translations.literal: His temperament was biased and eccentric; when his spirits were roused he would drink and compose poetry for days on end; when his mood flagged he would not even communicate with his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was biased and eccentric; when his spirits rose he would drink and write poetry for days; when his mood flagged he would not even speak with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，加前將軍，給油絡車，並給扶二人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Forward General and given a lacquered carriage with oiled canopy, along with two attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he was made Forward General and granted a lacquered carriage with oiled canopy, along with two men to support him.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王見害，鑠遷中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Prince Qiang of Poyang was killed, Shuo was transferred to Central Army General and Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Qiang of Poyang was killed, Shuo was transferred to Central Army General and Grand Minister with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 不自安，至東府見明帝，及出，處分存亡之計。

translations.literal: Feeling ill at ease, he went to the eastern residence to see Emperor Ming; when he came out he made arrangements for survival or destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in mind, he went to the eastern residence to see Emperor Ming; when he came out he set his affairs in order for life or death.

sentences.zh: 謂侍讀山悰曰：「吾前日覲王，王流涕嗚咽，而鄱陽、隨郡見誅。

translations.literal: He said to his attendant reader Shan Cong, "The other day when I paid respects to the king, the king wept and sobbed; yet Poyang and Sui commandery were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendant reader Shan Cong, "The other day when I visited the king, he wept and sobbed; yet Poyang and the Prince of Sui were killed.

sentences.zh: 今日見王，王又流涕而有愧色，其在吾邪？

translations.literal: Today when I see the king, he weeps again but with a guilty look—is it to be my turn?
translations.idiomatic: Today when I see the king, he weeps again but with a guilty expression—is it my turn?

sentences.zh: 」其夜三更中兵至，見害。

translations.literal: " That night at the third watch troops arrived and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: " That night at the third watch troops arrived and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 始興簡王鑒字宣徹，高帝第十子也。

translations.literal: Jian, Prince Jian of Shixing, style name Xuanche, was the tenth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Prince Jian of Shixing, whose style name was Xuanche, was Emperor Gao's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 性聰警。

translations.literal: His nature was clever and alert.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and perceptive by nature.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，喪所生母，號慕過人，數日中便至骨立。

translations.literal: At eight years he lost his birth mother; his mourning cries surpassed others', and within several days he was reduced to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he lost his birth mother; his cries of grief surpassed any adult's, and within days he was worn to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 豫章文獻王聞之，撫其首嗚咽，謂高帝曰：「此兒操行異人，恐其不濟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang heard of it, stroked his head and sobbed, and told Emperor Gao, "This boy's conduct is unlike others; I fear he may not survive.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang heard of it, stroked his head and wept, and told Emperor Gao, "This child's conduct is extraordinary; I fear he may not survive.

sentences.zh: 」高帝亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gao too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gao too was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 先是劫帥韓武方常聚黨千餘人，斷流為暴，郡縣不能禁，行旅斷絕。

translations.literal: Earlier the bandit chief Han Wufang had often gathered a party of over a thousand men, blocked the waterways and committed violence; the commanderies and counties could not restrain him and travelers ceased on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the bandit chief Han Wufang had gathered more than a thousand followers, blocked the waterways, and committed violence; commanderies and counties could not suppress him, and travel on the roads ceased.

sentences.zh: 鑒行至上明，武方乃出降。

translations.literal: When Jian's procession reached Shangming, Wufang came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's procession reached Shangming, Wufang came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 長史虞悰等咸請殺之。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Yu Yong and the rest all asked that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Yu Yong and the others all urged that he be killed.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「武方為暴積年，所在不能制，今降而被殺，失信；

translations.literal: Jian said, "Wufang has committed violence for many years; everywhere they could not control him; now that he has surrendered and is to be killed, faith is broken;
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Wufang has rampaged for years without local control; if we kill him now that he has surrendered, we break faith;

sentences.zh: 且無以勸善。

translations.literal: and there is no way to encourage goodness.
translations.idiomatic: and there is no way to encourage those who would do good.

sentences.zh: 」於是啟台，果被宥，自是巴西蠻夷凶惡，皆望風降附。

translations.literal: " He therefore reported to the provincial headquarters; Wufang was indeed pardoned, and from then on the fierce tribes of Baxi all submitted at the report of his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported to headquarters; Wufang was indeed pardoned, and thereafter the fierce tribes of Baxi all submitted at the news of his approach.

sentences.zh: 行次新城，道路籍籍，雲陳顯達大選士馬，不肯就征，巴西太守陰智伯亦以為然。

translations.literal: Passing Xincheng, the roads buzzed with reports that Chen Xianda was conscripting men and horses on a large scale and would not accept the summons; the Administrator of Baxi, Yin Zhibo, also thought this was so.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xincheng, travelers reported that Chen Xianda was conscripting men and horses on a large scale and refusing the summons; the Administrator of Baxi, Yin Zhibo, agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃停新城十許日，遣典簽張曇皙往觀形勢。

translations.literal: He therefore halted at Xincheng for some ten days and sent record-keeper Zhang Tanxi to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Xincheng for some ten days and sent chief clerk Zhang Tanxi to observe the situation.

sentences.zh: 俄而顯達遣使人郭安明、朱公恩奉書貢遺，咸勸鑒執之。

translations.literal: Before long Xianda sent envoys Guo Anming and Zhu Gong'en with letters and tribute gifts; all urged Jian to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianda sent envoys Guo Anming and Zhu Gong'en with letters and tribute; all urged Jian to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「顯達立節本朝，必自無此。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Xianda has established his integrity for this dynasty; he will certainly not do this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Xianda has stood loyal to this dynasty; he would certainly not do this.

sentences.zh: 曇皙還，若有同異，執安明等未晚。

translations.literal: When Tanxi returns, if there is anything amiss, arresting Anming and the rest will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanxi returns, if anything is amiss, arresting Anming and the rest will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」居二日，曇皙還，說顯達遣家累已出城，日夕望殿下至。

translations.literal: " After two days Tanxi returned and reported that Xianda had sent his family out of the city and from morning to evening awaited the prince's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: " Two days later Tanxi returned and reported that Xianda had sent his family out of the city and awaited the prince's arrival from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 於是乃前。

translations.literal: He therefore advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore advanced.

sentences.zh: 時年十四。

translations.literal: He was then fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fourteen years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文，不重華飾，器服清素，有高士風。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at composition, not valuing ornate display; his vessels and dress were plain, with the air of a lofty gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well, disdaining ornate display; his vessels and dress were plain, with the bearing of a lofty gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與記室參軍蔡仲熊登張儀樓，商略先言往行及蜀土人物。

translations.literal: With his secretarial aide Cai Zhongxiong he ascended the Zhang Yi tower and discussed former worthies and past conduct and the men of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: With his secretarial aide Cai Zhongxiong he climbed Zhang Yi Tower and discussed former worthies, past conduct, and the men of Shu.

sentences.zh: 鑒言辭和辯，仲熊應對無滯，當時以為盛事。

translations.literal: Jian's words were harmonious and eloquent; Zhongxiong's replies were unhesitating; at the time this was considered a splendid occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Jian spoke with grace and eloquence; Zhongxiong answered without hesitation; at the time it was considered a memorable occasion.

sentences.zh: 州城北門常閉不開，鑒問其故于虞悰，悰答曰：「蜀中多夷暴，有時抄掠至城下，故相承閉之。

translations.literal: The north gate of the provincial capital was regularly kept shut; Jian asked Yu Yong the reason; Yong answered, "Shu has many violent tribes; sometimes they raid to the foot of the walls, and therefore it has been kept closed by tradition.
translations.idiomatic: The north gate of the provincial capital was kept shut; Jian asked Yu Yong why; Yong said, "Shu has many violent tribes who sometimes raid to the city walls, so it has traditionally been kept closed.

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「古人云，'善閉無關楗'。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "The ancients said, 'Good closing needs no bar or bolt.'
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said, "The ancients said, 'When closing is done well, no bar or bolt is needed.'

sentences.zh: 且在德不在門。

translations.literal: It lies in virtue, not in gates.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in virtue, not in gates.

sentences.zh: 」即令開之。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered it opened.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered it opened.

sentences.zh: 戎夷慕義，自是清謐。

translations.literal: The tribes admired his righteousness, and from then on all was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes admired his righteousness, and thereafter the region was peaceful.

sentences.zh: 于州園地得古塚，無復棺，但有石槨。

translations.literal: In the provincial park an ancient tomb was found; there was no coffin remaining, only a stone outer coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the provincial park an ancient tomb was uncovered; no inner coffin remained, only a stone sarcophagus.

sentences.zh: 銅器十餘種，並古形；

translations.literal: More than ten kinds of bronze vessels, all of ancient form;
translations.idiomatic: More than ten kinds of bronze vessels, all of ancient form;

sentences.zh: 玉璧三枚；

translations.literal: three jade bi discs;
translations.idiomatic: three jade bi discs;

sentences.zh: 珍寶甚多，不可皆識；

translations.literal: many precious objects that could not all be identified;
translations.idiomatic: many precious objects that could not all be identified;

sentences.zh: 金銀為蠶蛇形者數斗。

translations.literal: gold and silver fashioned in the shapes of silkworms and serpents, several pecks in amount.
translations.idiomatic: gold and silver fashioned as silkworms and serpents, amounting to several pecks.

sentences.zh: 又以朱沙為阜，水銀為池，左右咸勸取之。

translations.literal: Cinnabar was piled as a mound and mercury as a pool; those on left and right all urged that they be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar was heaped as a mound and mercury formed a pool; those around him all urged that the treasures be taken.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「皇太子昔在雍，有發古塚者，得玉鏡、玉屏風、玉匣之屬，皆將還都，吾意常不同。

translations.literal: Jian said, "When the crown prince was formerly in Yong, an ancient tomb was opened and objects such as a jade mirror, jade screen, and jade casket were obtained—all were to be brought back to the capital; my view has always differed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "When the crown prince was in Yong, an ancient tomb was opened and a jade mirror, jade screen, jade casket, and the like were found—all were to be brought to the capital; I have always disagreed with this.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣功曹何佇為之起墳，諸寶物一不得犯。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent the merit officer He Zhu to build a mound over it; none of the precious objects was touched.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent merit officer He Zhu to rebuild the mound; not one precious object was touched.

sentences.zh: 性甚清，在蜀積年，未嘗有所營造，資用一歲不滿三萬。

translations.literal: His nature was very pure; during his years in Shu he never undertook any construction; his annual expenses did not amount to thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was exceptionally pure; during his years in Shu he undertook no construction; his annual expenses did not reach thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 王儉常歎云：「始興王雖尊貴，而行履都是素士。

translations.literal: Wang Jian often sighed and said, "Though the Prince of Shixing is exalted in rank, his conduct is entirely that of a plain scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian often sighed, "Though the Prince of Shixing is exalted in rank, his conduct is entirely that of a plain scholar.

sentences.zh: 」時有廣漢什邡人段祖，以錞於獻鑒，古禮器也。

translations.literal: " At the time Duan Zu of Shifang in Guanghan presented to Jian a chunyu—a ancient ritual vessel.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Duan Zu of Shifang in Guanghan presented to Jian a chunyu, an ancient ritual bell.

sentences.zh: 高三尺六寸六分，圍三尺四寸，圓如筩，銅色黑如漆，甚薄，上有銅馬，以繩縣馬，令去地尺餘，灌之以水，又以器盛水於下，以芒莖當心跪注淳於，以手振芒，則聲如雷，清響良久乃絕。

translations.literal: It was three chi six cun six fen in height, with a circumference of three chi four cun, round like a tube, the bronze black as lacquer and very thin; on top was a bronze horse, with a cord suspending the horse so it hung more than a chi above the ground; water was poured in, and a vessel of water placed below; a cogongrass stem was set at the center as a pivot, and when the hand shook the stem the sound was like thunder, the clear tone lasting long before dying away.
translations.idiomatic: It stood three chi six cun six fen high, with a circumference of three chi four cun, round as a tube, the bronze black as lacquer and very thin; atop it was a bronze horse suspended by a cord more than a chi above the ground; water was poured in and a vessel set below; a cogongrass stem served as the pivot at the center, and when the stem was shaken the sound was like thunder, the clear tone lingering long before fading.

sentences.zh: 古所以節樂也。

translations.literal: In antiquity it was used to regulate music.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity it was used to regulate music.

sentences.zh: 五年，鑒獻龍角一枚，長九尺三寸，色紅，有文。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jian presented a dragon horn one chi nine cun three fen long, red in color with markings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jian presented a dragon horn nine chi three cun long, red in color with markings.

sentences.zh: 江夏王鋒字宣穎，高帝第十二子也。

translations.literal: Feng, Prince of Jiangxia, style name Xuanying, was the twelfth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, Prince of Jiangxia, whose style name was Xuanying, was Emperor Gao's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 母張氏有容德，宋蒼梧王逼取之，又欲害鋒。

translations.literal: His mother the Zhang clan had beauty and virtue; Emperor Cangwu of Song forced her away and also wished to harm Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Zhang clan, possessed beauty and virtue; Emperor Cangwu of Song seized her by force and also wished to harm Feng.

sentences.zh: 高帝甚懼，不敢使居舊宅，匿于張氏舍，時年四歲。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao was greatly afraid and did not dare let him remain in the old residence, hiding him in the Zhang household; he was then four years old.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao was deeply afraid and dared not let him remain in the old residence, concealing him in the Zhang household; he was then four years old.

sentences.zh: 性方整，好學書，張家無紙劄，乃倚井欄為書，書滿則洗之，已復更書，如此者累月。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and square; he loved learning and writing; the Zhang family had no paper, so he leaned on the well railing to write, and when the railing was full he washed it and wrote again—thus for many months.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was upright; he loved learning and writing; the Zhang family had no paper, so he wrote on the well railing, washing it when full and writing again—thus for many months.

sentences.zh: 又晨興不肯拂窗塵，而先畫塵上，學為書字。

translations.literal: He also would not brush the window dust in the morning but first traced characters in the dust to practice writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the mornings he would not brush the window dust but first traced characters in the dust to practice writing.

sentences.zh: 五歲，高帝使學鳳尾諾，一學即工。

translations.literal: At five years Emperor Gao had him learn the phoenix-tail script; with one lesson he mastered it.
translations.idiomatic: At five Emperor Gao had him learn phoenix-tail script; with one lesson he mastered it.

sentences.zh: 高帝大悅，以玉騏驎賜之，曰：「騏驎賞鳳尾矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao was greatly pleased and bestowed on him a jade qilin, saying, "The qilin rewards the phoenix tail.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao was delighted and bestowed a jade qilin, saying, "The qilin rewards the phoenix tail.

sentences.zh: 」至十歲，便能屬文。

translations.literal: " By ten he could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: " By ten he could compose literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，藩邸嚴急，諸王不得讀異書，五經之外，唯得看孝子圖而已。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu the princely residences were strictly controlled; the princes might not read heterodox books—apart from the Five Classics they were permitted only the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the princely residences were strictly controlled; princes might not read unorthodox books—beyond the Five Classics they were permitted only the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 鋒乃密遣人於市里街巷買圖籍，期月之間，殆將備矣。

translations.literal: Feng secretly sent men to the market streets to buy illustrated books; within a month he had nearly assembled a full collection.
translations.idiomatic: Feng secretly sent men to the market streets to buy books; within a month he had nearly a complete library.

sentences.zh: 好琴書，蓋亦天性。

translations.literal: He loved the zither and books—this too was in his nature.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the zither and books—this too was his nature.

sentences.zh: 嘗覲武帝，賜以寶裝琴，仍於御前鼓之，大見賞。

translations.literal: He once had an audience with Emperor Wu, who bestowed on him a jeweled zither; he played before the emperor and was greatly admired.
translations.idiomatic: He once had an audience with Emperor Wu, who bestowed a jeweled zither; he played before the throne and was greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 帝謂鄱陽王鏘曰：「闍梨琴亦是柳令之流亞，其既事事有意，吾欲試以臨人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Prince Qiang of Poyang, "Cha Li's zither is also in the class of Magistrate Liu; in all things he shows intent—I wish to try him in governing men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Prince Qiang of Poyang, "Cha Li's zither ranks with Magistrate Liu; in everything he shows purpose—I wish to test him in governing men.

sentences.zh: 」鏘曰：「昔鄒忌鼓琴，威王委以國政。

translations.literal: " Qiang said, "In former times Zou Ji played the zither and King Wei entrusted him with the state's government.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiang said, "Long ago Zou Ji played the zither and King Wei of Qi entrusted him with the government.

sentences.zh: 」乃出為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was therefore sent out as Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was therefore sent out as Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 善與人交，行事王文和、別駕江祏等，皆相友善。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making friends; in conducting affairs he was on friendly terms with Wang Wenhe, the chief aide Jiang Shi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at friendship; in office he was close with Wang Wenhe, chief aide Jiang Shi, and others.

sentences.zh: 後文和被徵為益州，置酒告別，文和流淚曰：「下官少來未嘗作詩，今日違戀，不覺文生於性。

translations.literal: Later Wenhe was summoned to Yizhou; at the farewell banquet Wenhe wept and said, "Your servant from youth has never composed poetry; today at this parting, unawares, literature was born from my nature.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenhe was summoned to Yizhou; at the farewell banquet he wept and said, "I have never composed poetry in my life; today at this parting, literature sprang unawares from my nature.

sentences.zh: 」王儉聞之，曰：「江夏可謂善變素絲也。」

translations.literal: " Wang Jian heard of it and said, "Jiangxia may be said to transform plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian heard of it and said, "Jiangxia can truly transform plain silk.

sentences.zh: 工書，為當時蕃王所推。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calligraphy and was esteemed among the princes of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at calligraphy and was esteemed among the princes of his day.

sentences.zh: 南郡王昭業亦稱工，謂武帝曰：「臣書固應勝江夏王。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaoye of Nankang also claimed skill and told Emperor Wu, "Your servant's writing should surely surpass the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhaoye of Nankang also claimed skill and told Emperor Wu, "My writing should surely surpass the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 」武帝答：「闍梨第一，法身第二。

translations.literal: " The emperor answered, "Cha Li is first, Dharma Body second.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "Cha Li is first, Dharma Body second.

sentences.zh: 」法身昭業小名，闍梨鋒小名也。

translations.literal: " Dharma Body was Zhaoye's childhood name; Cha Li was Feng's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Dharma Body was Zhaoye's childhood name; Cha Li was Feng's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，為侍中，領驍騎將軍，尋加秘書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also made Director of the Secretariat Archives.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also Director of the Secretariat Archives.

sentences.zh: 及明帝知權，蕃邸危懼，江祏嘗謂王晏曰：「江夏王有才行，亦善能匿跡，以琴道授羊景之，景之著名，而江夏掩能於世，非唯七弦而已，百氏亦復如之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming grasped power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once said to Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has ability and conduct and is also skilled at concealing his talents; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his ability from the world. It is not only in the seven strings; the hundred schools are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming seized power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once told Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has talent and conduct and excels at concealing his abilities; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his skill from the world. It is not only the seven strings; the hundred schools are the same.

sentences.zh: 」鋒聞歎曰：「江祏遂復為混沌畫眉，欲益反弊耳。

translations.literal: " When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—he means to help but will only make things worse.
translations.idiomatic: " When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—intending to help, he will only make things worse.

sentences.zh: 寡人聲酒是耽，狗馬是好，豈復一豪于平生哉。

translations.literal: I am devoted to sound and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I be a hair's breadth different from my whole life?
translations.idiomatic: I am devoted to music and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I change a hair's breadth from the life I have always lived?

sentences.zh: 」當時以為話言。

translations.literal: " At the time this was taken as a saying.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time this was taken as a memorable saying.

sentences.zh: 常忽忽不樂，著修柏賦以見志，曰：「既殊群而抗立，亦含貞而挺正。

translations.literal: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent, saying, "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds steadfastness and stands upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent: "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds to integrity and stands upright.

sentences.zh: 豈春日之自芳，在霜下而為盛。

translations.literal: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes under frost.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes beneath the frost.

sentences.zh: 沖風不能摧其枝，積雪不能改其性。

translations.literal: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.

sentences.zh: 雖坎壇于當年，庶後凋之可詠。

translations.literal: Though it may be cut down in its season, later decline may still be sung of.
translations.idiomatic: Though cut down in its season, its later withering may still be worthy of song.

sentences.zh: 」時鼎業潛移，鋒獨慨然有匡復之意，逼之行事典簽，故不遂也。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper pressed him, and therefore he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper constrained him, and so he did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 嘗見明帝，言次及遙光才力可委之意，鋒答曰：「遙光之于殿下，猶殿下之于高皇，衛宗廟，安社稷，實有攸寄。

translations.literal: He once saw Emperor Ming and in conversation touched on the idea that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the altars of soil and grain: the charge is real.
translations.idiomatic: He once saw Emperor Ming and in passing mentioned that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the state: the charge is real.

sentences.zh: 」明帝失色。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming turned pale.

sentences.zh: 鋒有武力，明帝殺諸王，鋒與書詰責，左右不為通。

translations.literal: Feng had martial strength; when Emperor Ming killed the princes, Feng wrote a letter rebuking him, but those around would not pass it through.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had martial strength; when Emperor Ming killed the princes, Feng wrote a letter of rebuke, but his attendants would not deliver it.

sentences.zh: 明帝深憚之，不敢於第收之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming deeply feared him and did not dare seize him at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming deeply feared him and did not dare seize him at his residence.

sentences.zh: 鋒出登車，兵人欲上車防勒，鋒以手擊卻數人，皆應時倒地，遂逼害之。

translations.literal: When Feng went out and mounted his carriage, soldiers wished to board the carriage to restrain him; Feng struck several men with his hand and they fell to the ground at once; he was then forced to his death.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng went out and mounted his carriage, soldiers tried to board and restrain him; Feng struck several men with his hand and they fell instantly; he was then killed.

sentences.zh: 江斅聞其死，流涕曰：「芳蘭當門，不得不鋤，其修柏之賦乎。」

translations.literal: Jiang Jiao heard of his death and wept, saying, "When fragrant orchids stand at the gate, they must be uprooted—is it not his fu on the evergreen cypress?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiao heard of his death and wept, saying, "When fragrant orchids stand at the gate, they must be uprooted—is it not his fu on the evergreen cypress?"

sentences.zh: 南平王銳字宣毅，高帝第十五子也。

translations.literal: Rui, Prince of Nanping, style name Xuanyi, was the fifteenth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, Prince of Nanping, whose style name was Xuanyi, was Emperor Gao's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 位左戶尚書，朝直勤謹，未嘗屬疾。

translations.literal: He held the post of Minister of the Left Household; at court he was diligent and careful and never claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Left Household; at court he was diligent and careful and never claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，出為南中郎將、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he was sent out as Southern Central Army General and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he was sent out as Southern Central Army General and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，明帝作輔，害諸王，遣裴叔業平尋陽，仍進湘州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming acted as regent and killed the princes, he sent Pei Shuye to pacify Xunyang and then advance into Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming acted as regent and killed the princes, he sent Pei Shuye to pacify Xunyang and then advance into Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 銳防合周伯玉大言於眾曰：「此非天子意，今斬叔業，舉兵匡社稷，誰敢不同！

translations.literal: Rui's defense coordinator Zhou Boyu spoke loudly before the assembly: "This is not the Son of Heaven's intent; now if we behead Shuye and raise troops to restore the altars, who would dare not follow!
translations.idiomatic: Rui's defense coordinator Zhou Boyu declared before the assembly: "This is not the Son of Heaven's will; if we behead Shuye now and raise troops to restore the altars, who would dare refuse!

sentences.zh: 」銳典簽叱左右斬之，銳見害，伯玉下獄誅。

translations.literal: " Rui's record-keeper shouted for the attendants to behead him; Rui was killed and Boyu was imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui's chief clerk ordered the attendants to behead Boyu; Rui was killed and Boyu was imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 宜都王鏗字宣儼，高帝第十六子也。

translations.literal: Qiang, Prince of Yidu, style name Xuanyan, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang, Prince of Yidu, whose style name was Xuanyan, was Emperor Gao's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 生三歲喪母。

translations.literal: At three years he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 及有識，問母所在，左右告以早亡，便思慕蔬食自悲。

translations.literal: When he came to awareness he asked where his mother was; those around told him she had died early, and he mourned her with plain food and private grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to awareness he asked where his mother was; his attendants told him she had died young, and he mourned with plain food and private grief.

sentences.zh: 不識母，常祈請幽冥，求一夢見。

translations.literal: Not knowing his mother, he often prayed in the nether world, seeking to dream of her once.
translations.idiomatic: Never having known his mother, he often prayed in the unseen world, seeking one dream of her.

sentences.zh: 至六歲，遂夢見一女人，雲是其母。

translations.literal: At six years he did dream of a woman who said she was his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At six he dreamed of a woman who said she was his mother.

sentences.zh: 鏗悲泣向舊左右說容貌衣服事，皆如平生，聞者莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: Qiang wept and told the old attendants her appearance and clothing; all were as in life, and those who heard were moved to sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang wept and described her appearance and clothing to his old attendants; all matched her in life, and those who heard were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 清悟有學行。

translations.literal: Clear-minded and perceptive, with learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was clear-minded and perceptive, with learning and proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，為南豫州刺史、都督二州軍事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming he became Inspector of Southern Yuzhou and supervised military affairs of the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongming he was appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou with authority over military affairs in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 雖未經庶務，而雅得人心。

translations.literal: Though he had not yet handled routine affairs, he naturally won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had not yet handled routine administration, he naturally won people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 舉動每為簽帥所制，立意多不得行。

translations.literal: His every move was controlled by the record-keeper; many of his intentions could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: His every move was controlled by the chief clerk; many of his intentions could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 州鎮姑孰，于時人發桓溫女塚，得金巾箱，織金篾為嚴器，又有金蠶銀繭等物甚多。

translations.literal: The provincial seat was at Gushu; at the time someone opened the tomb of Huan Wen's daughter and obtained a gold kerchief box and vessels woven of gold strips, along with many objects such as gold silkworms and silver cocoons.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial seat was at Gushu; at the time someone opened the tomb of Huan Wen's daughter and found a gold kerchief box and vessels woven of gold strips, along with many objects such as gold silkworms and silver cocoons.

sentences.zh: 條以啟聞，郁林敕以物賜之。

translations.literal: He listed them in a memorial; Emperor Yulin ordered the objects given to him.
translations.idiomatic: He listed them in a memorial; Emperor Yulin ordered the objects given to him.

sentences.zh: 鏗曰：「今取往物，後取今物，如此回圈，豈可不熟念。

translations.literal: Qiang said, "If we take objects from the past, later others will take objects from the present—such a cycle—how can one not think carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang said, "If we take objects from the past, later others will take objects from the present—in such a cycle, how can one not think carefully?

sentences.zh: 」使長史蔡約自往修復，纖毫不犯。

translations.literal: " He had chief administrator Cai Yue go in person to restore it; not the slightest thing was touched.
translations.idiomatic: " He had chief administrator Cai Yue go in person to restore the tomb; not the slightest thing was touched.

sentences.zh: 年十歲時，與吉景曜商略先言往行。

translations.literal: At ten years he discussed with Ji Jingyao the former worthies and past conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he discussed with Ji Jingyao the former worthies and past conduct.

sentences.zh: 左右誤排柟榴屏風，倒壓其背，顏色不異，言談無輟，亦不顧視。

translations.literal: An attendant mistakenly knocked over a nanmu and pomegranate screen, which fell and pressed his back; his expression did not change, his talk did not pause, and he did not even look around.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant mistakenly knocked over a nanmu and pomegranate screen, which fell on his back; his expression did not change, his conversation did not pause, and he did not even look around.

sentences.zh: 彌善射，常以堋的太闊，曰：「終日射侯，何難之有。

translations.literal: He was exceptionally skilled at archery and often said the target butt was too wide: "Shooting at the mark all day—what difficulty is there?
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at archery and often said the target butt was too wide: "Shooting at the mark all day—what difficulty is there?

sentences.zh: 」乃取甘蔗插地，百步射之，十發十中。

translations.literal: " He took sugarcane stalks, stuck them in the ground, and shot at them from a hundred paces—ten shots, ten hits.
translations.idiomatic: " He stuck sugarcane stalks in the ground and shot at them from a hundred paces—ten shots, ten hits.

sentences.zh: 永明中，制諸王年未三十，不得畜妾。

translations.literal: During Yongming a regulation was made that princes not yet thirty might not keep concubines.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming a regulation was made that princes under thirty might not keep concubines.

sentences.zh: 及武帝晏駕後，有勸取左右者，鏗曰：「在內不無使役，既先朝遺旨，何忍而違。」

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu's death some urged him to take attendants; Qiang said, "Within the residence there are inevitably servants; since this was the former emperor's last command, how can I bear to violate it."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu's death some urged him to take concubines; Qiang said, "Within the residence there are inevitably servants; since this was the former emperor's last command, how can I bear to violate it?"

sentences.zh: 及延興元年，明帝誅高、武、文惠諸子，鏗聞之，馮左右從容雅步，詠陸機吊魏武云：「昔以四海為己任，死則以愛子托人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, leaning on his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Emperor Wu of Wei: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, supported by his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Cao Cao: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another.

sentences.zh: 」如此者三，左右皆泣。

translations.literal: " He did this three times; those around all wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He did this three times; all around him wept.

sentences.zh: 後果遣呂文顯賚藥往，夜進聽事，正逢八關齋。

translations.literal: Later Lü Wenxian was indeed sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Wenxian was sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.

sentences.zh: 鏗上高坐，謂文顯曰：「高皇昔寵任君，何事乃有今日之行？

translations.literal: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why today's action?
translations.idiomatic: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why this action today?

sentences.zh: 」答云：「出不獲已。

translations.literal: " He answered, "I could not do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 」於是仰藥。

translations.literal: " He therefore swallowed the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore swallowed the medicine.

sentences.zh: 時年十八。

translations.literal: He was then eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，鏗狀似兄嶷，咸以國器許之。

translations.literal: He stood seven chi in height; Qiang's appearance resembled his elder brother Ying, and all regarded him as material for the state.
