translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi tall; Qiang resembled his elder brother Ying in appearance, and all regarded him as fit for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 及死，有識者莫不痛惜。

translations.literal: At his death all who knew him grieved.
translations.idiomatic: At his death all who knew him grieved.

sentences.zh: 初鏗出合時，年七歲，陶弘景為侍讀，八九年中，甚相接遇。

translations.literal: When Qiang first left the palace compound he was seven years old; Tao Hongjing served as his reader and for eight or nine years they were much in contact.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang first left the palace compound he was seven; Tao Hongjing served as his reader, and for eight or nine years they were much in contact.

sentences.zh: 後弘景隱山，忽夢鏗來，慘然言別，云：「某日命過。

translations.literal: Later Hongjing retired to the mountains; suddenly he dreamed Qiang came, speaking mournfully of parting, saying, "On such-and-such a day my life will end.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hongjing retired to the mountains; suddenly he dreamed Qiang came, speaking mournfully of parting, saying, "On such-and-such a day my allotted life will end.

sentences.zh: 身無罪，後三年當生某家。

translations.literal: I am without guilt; three years hence I will be born in such-and-such a family.
translations.idiomatic: I am without guilt; three years hence I will be born into such-and-such a family.

sentences.zh: 」弘景訪以幽中事，多秘不出。

translations.literal: Hongjing questioned him about affairs in the nether world; he mostly kept secrets and would not reveal them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing questioned him about affairs in the nether world; he mostly kept secrets and would not reveal them.

sentences.zh: 覺後，即遣信出都參訪，果與事符同，弘景因著夢記云。

translations.literal: After waking he at once sent a messenger to the capital to investigate; it matched the events exactly, and Hongjing therefore wrote a record of the dream.
translations.idiomatic: After waking he sent a messenger to the capital to investigate; it matched the events exactly, and Hongjing therefore wrote a record of the dream.

sentences.zh: 河東王鉉字宣胤，高帝第十九子也。

translations.literal: Xuan, Prince of Hedong, style name Xuanyin, was the nineteenth son of Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, Prince of Hedong, whose style name was Xuanyin, was Emperor Gao's nineteenth son.

sentences.zh: 母張氏，有寵于高帝，鉉又最幼，尤所留心。

translations.literal: His mother the Zhang clan was favored by Emperor Gao; Xuan was also the youngest, and he was especially attentive to him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Zhang clan, was favored by Emperor Gao; Xuan was also the youngest, and he paid special attention to him.

sentences.zh: 高帝臨崩，以屬武帝，武帝甚加意焉，為納柳世隆女為妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao was on his deathbed he entrusted Xuan to Emperor Wu; Wu paid him very special attention and married him to the daughter of Liu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Gao entrusted Xuan to Emperor Wu; Wu paid him very special attention and married him to the daughter of Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 武帝與群臣看新婦，流涕不自勝，豫章王嶷亦哽咽。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu and the ministers viewed the new bride; he wept uncontrollably, and the Prince of Yuzhang also choked with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu and the ministers viewed the new bride; he wept uncontrollably, and the Prince of Yuzhang also choked with sobs.

sentences.zh: 及明帝誅高帝諸子，以鉉高帝所愛，亦以才弱年幼，故得全。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming killed the sons of Emperor Gao, because Xuan was beloved by Emperor Gao and was also weak in talent and young in years, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming killed Emperor Gao's sons, because Xuan was beloved by Emperor Gao and was also weak in talent and young, he was spared.

sentences.zh: 初鉉年三四歲，高帝嘗晝臥纏發，鉉上高帝腹上弄繩，高帝因以繩賜鉉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuan was three or four years old, Emperor Gao was once napping with his hair bound up; Xuan climbed onto Emperor Gao's belly to play with the cord, and Emperor Gao therefore gave the cord to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xuan was three or four, Emperor Gao was napping with his hair bound up; Xuan climbed onto his belly to play with the cord, and Emperor Gao gave him the cord.

sentences.zh: 及崩後，鉉以寶函盛繩，歲時輒開視，流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: After the emperor's death Xuan kept the cord in a jeweled casket and each year at the proper season would open it and view it, weeping and sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death Xuan kept the cord in a jeweled casket and each year at the proper season would open it to view, weeping and sobbing.

sentences.zh: 人才甚凡，而有此一至。

translations.literal: His talent was very ordinary, yet he had this one excellence.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was very ordinary, yet he had this one excellence.

sentences.zh: 建武中，高、武子孫憂疑。

translations.literal: During Jianwu the descendants of Gao and Wu were anxious and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu the descendants of Gao and Wu were anxious and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 鉉朝見，常鞠躬俯僂，不敢正行直視。

translations.literal: When Xuan attended court he constantly bowed low and stooped, not daring to walk straight or look directly ahead.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan attended court he constantly bowed low and stooped, not daring to walk straight or look directly ahead.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中、衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Guard General.

sentences.zh: 鉉年稍長。

translations.literal: Xuan gradually grew older.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan gradually grew older.

sentences.zh: 四年，誅王晏，以謀立鉉為名，鉉免官，以王還第，禁不得與外人交通。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden to have contact with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden contact with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，明帝疾暴甚，乃見害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened greatly, and Xuan was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened sharply, and Xuan was then killed.

sentences.zh: 聞收至，欣然曰：「死生命也，終不斅建安乞為奴而不得。

translations.literal: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and not succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and failing.

sentences.zh: 」仰藥而卒。

translations.literal: He swallowed the medicine and died.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed the medicine and died.

sentences.zh: 鉉二子在孩抱，亦見殺。

translations.literal: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：豫章文獻王珪璋之質，夙表天姿，行己所安，率由忠敬。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The Prince of Yuzhang possessed the quality of a ceremonial jade scepter; from early on he showed heaven's endowment; in what he practiced he was at ease, always following loyalty and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The Prince of Yuzhang possessed the quality of a ceremonial jade scepter; from early on he showed heaven's endowment; in conduct he followed what was right, always through loyalty and reverence.

sentences.zh: 雖代宗之議早隆皇矚，而天倫之愛無虧永明，故知「為仁由己」，不虛言也。

translations.literal: Though the deliberation on the heir of the dynasty was early honored in the imperial gaze, the love of the heavenly kin was not diminished in Yongming; thus one knows that "benevolence comes from oneself" is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Though deliberation on the heir was early honored in the imperial gaze, affection within the family was not diminished in Yongming; thus one knows that "benevolence comes from oneself" is no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 自宋受晉終，馬氏遂為廢姓，齊受宋禪，劉宗盡見誅夷，梁武革齊，弗取前轍，子恪兄弟，並皆錄用，雖見梁武之弘裕，亦表文獻之余慶。

translations.literal: From the time Song received the end of Jin the house of Ma became a discarded surname; when Qi received the abdication of Song the Liu clan was entirely exterminated; when Liang Wu overturned Qi he did not follow the previous track—the brothers Zike and the rest were all employed; though this shows Liang Wu's magnanimity, it also manifests the remaining blessing of the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Song received Jin's end the house of Ma became a discarded surname; when Qi received Song's abdication the Liu clan was entirely exterminated; when Liang Wu overturned Qi he did not follow the previous course—the brothers Zike and the rest were all employed; though this shows Liang Wu's magnanimity, it also manifests the remaining blessing of the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 昔陳思表云：「權之所存，雖疏必重，勢之所去，雖親必輕。

translations.literal: In former times Chen Si wrote in a memorial: "Where power resides, though distant one must treat as weighty; where power departs, though close one must treat as light.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Chen Si wrote in a memorial: "Where power resides, though distant one must treat as weighty; where power departs, though close one must treat as light.

sentences.zh: 」原夫此言，實存固本。

translations.literal: " Considering this saying, it truly exists to strengthen the root.
translations.idiomatic: " Considering this saying, it truly exists to strengthen the root.

sentences.zh: 然就國之典，既隨代革，卿士入朝，作貴蕃輔，皇王托體，同稟尊極，仕無常資，秩有恆數，禮地兼隆，易生推擬。

translations.literal: Yet the institution of princely states changed with each dynasty; ministers entering court became honored assistants in the provinces; imperial princes as embodiments of the body shared the same exalted parentage; offices had no fixed stipend, ranks had constant numbers; ritual status was doubly elevated, and rivalry easily arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the institution of princely states changed with each dynasty; ministers entering court became honored assistants in the provinces; imperial princes as embodiments of the body shared the same exalted parentage; offices had no fixed stipend, ranks had constant numbers; ritual status was doubly elevated, and rivalry easily arose.

sentences.zh: 武帝顧命，情深尊嫡，密圖遠算，意在求安。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's deathbed charge was deep in honoring the direct heir; his secret plans and far-reaching calculations aimed at seeking security.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's deathbed charge deeply honored the direct heir; his secret plans and far-reaching calculations aimed at securing the state.

sentences.zh: 以明帝同起布衣，用存顧托，遂韜末命于近戚，寄重任於疏親。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Ming rose together from common cloth, he kept the late emperor's trust in mind and therefore concealed the final command among close kin, entrusting heavy responsibility to distant kin.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Ming rose together from common cloth, he kept the late emperor's trust in mind and therefore concealed the final command among close kin, entrusting heavy responsibility to distant kin.

sentences.zh: 以為子弟布列，外有強大之固，支庶中立，可息覬覦之謀，表裏相維，洊隆家國。

translations.literal: He thought that with sons and younger brothers arrayed, outwardly there would be a strong solid defense and among the branch lines a central stand could quell schemes of covetous watching; inside and outside mutually sustaining, the house and state would repeatedly rise.
translations.idiomatic: He thought that with sons and younger brothers arrayed, outwardly there would be a strong defense and among the branch lines a central stand could quell covetous schemes; inside and outside mutually sustaining, the house and state would repeatedly prosper.

sentences.zh: 曾不慮機能運衡，權可制眾，宗族殲滅，一至於斯。

translations.literal: He never considered that when ability can turn the balance and power can control the multitude, the clan kin would be annihilated—to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He never considered that when ability can turn the balance and power can control the multitude, the clan kin would be annihilated—to this degree.

sentences.zh: 曹植之言，遠有致矣。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi's words had far-reaching application indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi's words had far-reaching application indeed.
